evidence.title: Total loss of circulation in fractured Barail sandstone
evidence.description: Total loss of circulation encountered at 3150m while drilling through fractured Barail sandstone. Mud weight was 1.42 sg. Lost 45 m³ of OBM over 6 hours.
evidence.root_cause: Natural fractures in Barail sandstone exacerbated by high ECD (1.52 sg).
evidence.mitigation: Reduced mud weight to 1.38 sg, pumped LCM pills (calcium carbonate + graphite), cured losses after 18 hours.
evidence.lessons: Keep ECD ≤1.48 sg between 3,100 and 3,250 m, pre-treat with 15 ppb background LCM before 3,140 m and drill the interval at reduced flow rate.

evidence.title: Partial losses in Barail sandstone
evidence.description: Partial losses of 8–12 m³/hr at 3,172 m; 38 m³ lost in total.
evidence.root_cause: Induced fractures in Barail sandstone at an ECD of 1.51 sg.
evidence.mitigation: Reduced flow rate from 2,050 to 1,750 l/min and pumped a 60 ppb LCM pill; losses healed in 5 hours.
evidence.lessons: Drill the Barail between 3,150 and 3,220 m with ECD below 1.48 sg.

evidence.title: Stuck pipe (differential sticking) during connection
evidence.description: Pipe stuck at 3400m during connection. Overpull of 80 kN. Shale swelling observed in cuttings.
evidence.root_cause: Reactive Kopili shale swelling due to inadequate KCl inhibition in mud system. Hole left open for 45 minutes during BHA change.
evidence.mitigation: Spotted 15 m³ of diesel-based spotting fluid, worked pipe for 12 hours, freed at 120 kN overpull. Increased KCl to 7% in mud system.
evidence.lessons: Maintain KCl ≥7% before entering the Kopili, keep static time under 15 minutes and spot a pill before BHA changes.

evidence.title: Mechanical sticking at key seat
evidence.description: Mechanical sticking at 3410m due to key seating in dogleg. Torque increased from 12 kN·m to 28 kN·m over 30 minutes.
evidence.root_cause: Key seat formation at 3400m dogleg (8°/30m). Insufficient reaming during trip out.
evidence.mitigation: Back-reamed to 3350m, reamed down with under-reamer, freed pipe. Modified tripping procedures to include reaming every stand.
evidence.lessons: Keep doglegs below 5°/30 m in the Kopili and ream every stand when tripping through it.

evidence.title: Momentary stuck pipe on connection
evidence.description: Pipe stuck momentarily on a connection at 3,402 m with 150 kN overpull; worked free in 2 hours.
evidence.root_cause: Swelling Kopili shale with KCl depleted to 4.5%.
evidence.mitigation: Worked pipe with jars and freed it in 2 hours; KCl restored to 7%.
evidence.lessons: Check KCl every tour while in the Kopili.

mud_window.note: Offset-calibrated window 1.36–1.76 sg: keep mud weight ≥ 1.39 sg and ECD ≤ 1.75 sg.

brief.method: Projected severity scores each window with the bit at its top from offset history only (live-parameter factor = 0); likelihood = offsets that hit the window ÷ offsets drilled to that depth; expected NPT = likelihood × mean NPT per affected offset.

model.name: NWIS explainable hybrid risk score

factors.proximity: 1.0 inside the offset event window; up to 0.5 when approaching (linear over 150 m); decays after passing.
factors.frequency: Distinct offset wells within the radius with this event in the window ÷ 5 (capped at 1).
factors.similarity: Mean well-similarity (formations, coverage, trajectory, parameters, distance) of those offsets.
factors.formation: 1.0 when drilling the zone formation; 0.5 within 50 m above its prognosed top.
factors.parameter: Share of the risk family's live signals flagged against programme / rolling baseline / offset limits.
factors.trajectory: Inclination match with the offset well at the event depth.

model.alert_policy: High/critical-history zones alert at ≥0.55; medium/low-history zones alert only at ≥0.75 (live signal confirmation). Below that, the assessment is shown as a watch card.
limitations: Rule-weighted — scores rank risk, they are not probabilities. The learned model below is a cross-check, not the alert driver.
The demo field is illustrative; weights must be tuned on authorised OIL history before operational use.
Decision support only — the engineer remains the decision maker.

learned.method: L2-regularised logistic regression on the six risk factors (Newton/IRLS, pure Python)
learned.target: offset well recorded the risk family within 50 m ahead of the bit (or at the bit)
learned.validation: leave-one-well-out backtest over completed offset wells
learned.caveat: Trained on the synthetic demo field — it demonstrates the calibration method; retrain on authorised OIL history before operational use. The hand-set score remains the alert driver.

spotcheck.method: Held-out spot-check. The prose rules were tuned on the Sleipner–Volve–Johan Sverdrup study area (quadrants 15–16) and then frozen. Every k-th extraction (ordered by key) from wellbores OUTSIDE that area was read against its source sentence. Verdicts: correct = a real drilling incident of the stated type, at the stated depth when one is given; depth_off = right incident, wrong depth; not_event = not an incident of this well. Precision only — incidents the extractor missed are not counted (recall is not measured). Labels are reproducible: the key is sha1(well|sentence)[:10].

rows.evidence: The unexpected large amounts of sand caused operational problems due to instability and the drill string got stuck at 1086 m, on 17 August. The string was backed off and the well was re-spudded on 18 August. The casing program was re-designed to penetrate and stabilize the sandy Utsira Formation and Hordaland Group with a weighted mud system.

rows.label: Stuck Pipe
rows.sentence: At 5936 m the BHA became stuck while drilling the Sandnes Formation.
rows.evidence: At 5936 m the BHA became stuck while drilling the Sandnes Formation. The well was subsequently sidetracked to 9/2-8S T2 from 5680 m on the 4 October 1997. The T2 sidetrack was only drilled to 6011 m due to the BHA becoming stuck at 6002 m while pulling out of hole.
rows.cause: The T2 sidetrack was only drilled to 6011 m due to the BHA becoming stuck at 6002 m while pulling out of hole.

rows.label: Kick
rows.sentence: The first well in the block, well 2/1-1 drilled in 1972, was abandoned after taking a kick in the Late Jurassic.
rows.evidence: The first well in the block, well 2/1-1 drilled in 1972, was abandoned after taking a kick in the Late Jurassic. The second well, well 2/1-2 drilled in1978 encountered water wet Late Jurassic sandstones. The 2/1-3 well was drilled in 1980 on the downthrown side of a NW-SE trending fault complex and found oil in a 60 m thick Late Jurassic sandstone.
rows.note: Describes the kick in an earlier well (2/1-1), not this one.

rows.label: Kick
rows.sentence: While pulling out of the hole, following the cutting core to a depth of 4357.1 m, an influx of gas occurred and the well was shut in.
rows.evidence: While pulling out of the hole, following the cutting core to a depth of 4357.1 m, an influx of gas occurred and the well was shut in. Following a 22 hours well kill operation, the well was brought back under control.

rows.label: Wellbore Instability
rows.sentence: The drilling went forth without incident except for gumbo problems in the top of the 17 1/2" section and minor problems with tight hole in the 8 3/8" section.
rows.evidence: The drilling went forth without incident except for gumbo problems in the top of the 17 1/2" section and minor problems with tight hole in the 8 3/8" section. The well was drilled with sea water and hi-vis pills down to 615 m and with KCl/Drispac mud from 615 m to 2115 m. From 2115 m to TD the well was drilled with KCl/Drispac mud, converted to a fully dispersed gel-lignosulphonate mud in the limestone section.
